text:
maria_g: Customer outage — SSO logins started failing right after they published new IdP metadata. They see immediate 403s, and our logs show `No matching ACS found` when we validate the incoming AuthnRequest. Metadata URL they gave: https://idp.customer-corp/example-metadata.xml

vikram_r: pulling metadata now. can you paste the failing saml trace from our auth logs?

maria_g: pasted below. error goes back to 2026-03-10 20:12 UTC.

```
2026-03-10T20:12:02Z auth.saml: WARN - incoming AuthnRequest AssertionConsumerServiceURL=https://app.customer-corp/sso/consume, no ACS matched in configured SP metadata
2026-03-10T20:12:02Z auth.saml: ERROR - SamlValidationError: ACS-mismatch
    at SamlValidator.matchACS (/opt/redwood/saml/validator.js:342:21)
    at processRequest (/opt/redwood/saml/handler.js:88:13)
```

eng-saml: quick note — we recently tightened ACS parsing to reject relative/ambiguous URLs; that might be related. do we still have their old metadata cached?

alex_k: they switched metadata endpoints earlier today. i grabbed both copies. old metadata (2026-03-09): contains absolute ACS `https://app.customer-corp/sso/consume` and a KeyDescriptor with <ds:X509Certificate> base64 cert block. new metadata (2026-03-10): looks odd — there is an `xml:base` on the <EntityDescriptor> and ACS entries are relative paths, e.g. `/sso/consume`. also KeyDescriptor ordering changed and the cert is wrapped with extra line breaks and leading spaces. snippet: 

```
<EntityDescriptor entityID="https://idp.customer-corp" xml:base="https://idp.customer-corp">
  <SPSSODescriptor>
    <AssertionConsumerService Binding="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:bindings:HTTP-POST" Location="/sso/consume" index="0"/>
    ...
  </SPSSODescriptor>
  <KeyDescriptor use="signing">
    <KeyInfo>
      <X509Data>
        <X509Certificate>
          MIIF ... (many whitespace + linefeeds inserted here)
        </X509Certificate>
      </X509Data>
    </KeyInfo>
  </KeyDescriptor>
</EntityDescriptor>
```

maria_g: so our parser currently treats Location values as absolute when they start with "http" and otherwise rejects relative ones for security. the customer's AuthnRequest included absolute ACS (https://app.customer-corp/sso/consume) but our SP metadata parser kept the configured ACS as "/sso/consume" because of the xml:base — when we compared them we did a strict equality and failed.

vikram_r: that makes sense. reproduction steps: fetch metadata, run our metadata-normalizer and then run the ACS matcher with the sample AuthnRequest. i can repro locally with the new metadata file.

```
curl -sS https://idp.customer-corp/example-metadata.xml > /tmp/metadata.xml
node tools/saml-normalizer.js /tmp/metadata.xml > /tmp/normalized.json
node tools/saml-validate-acs.js --sp /tmp/normalized.json --authn-request samples/authn_https_acs.xml
```

eng-saml: thanks. two issues here: 1) `xml:base` resolution wasn't applied by our normalizer (bug), 2) we also strip-and-compare ACS strings which fails when one side is absolute and the other is relative-with-base. additionally the KeyDescriptor whitespace in the certificate caused our cert fingerprint extractor to error intermittently (`Invalid base64`). that explains sporadic cert-not-found errors in other customer logs.

alex_k: workaround suggestions for the customer: 1) ask their IdP admin to publish absolute ACS URLs (fastest), or 2) set a temporary manual ACS override in the org admin console (we can push a UI change per-org), or 3) we can fetch their metadata and normalize xml:base server-side and upload a cleaned copy to their tenant record (manual support action).

maria_g: customer is asking for ETA. what's the quickest fix we can do without code deploy?

eng-saml: immediate support action: we can upload a cleaned metadata blob to their tenant record (option 3). i'll run the normalizer script locally, fix base resolution and cert whitespace, and paste back the cleaned XML. no infra deploy needed. medium-term: patch normalizer and add xml:base resolution + tolerant ACS matching in our next patch release.

vikram_r: i'm creating a short-lived runbook for oncall:
- fetch metadata URL (curl)
- run normalizer with `--resolve-xml-base` flag (we'll ship this binary to oncall temporarily)
- validate with sample AuthnRequest
- if passes, upload cleaned metadata to tenant via admin API `POST /admin/tenants/:id/metadata`

maria_g: please add the admin API call snippet and I'll share with the customer ops team.

vikram_r: admin upload example: 
```
curl -X POST "https://console.redwood.ai/admin/tenants/12345/metadata" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_API_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/xml" \
  --data-binary @/tmp/metadata-cleaned.xml
```

support-bot: incident created: INC-2026-2794 (priority P2) — assigned to eng-saml.

eng-saml: putting a note: PR will include xml:base resolution, trim/compact cert base64, and fallback ACS comparison (resolve and compare normalized absolute URLs). target patch for 2026-03-12 deploy window. i'll include tests with metadata that use xml:base and relative ACS entries.

maria_g: thanks. i'll reply to customer with the temporary upload option + ETA for fix. posting the normalized metadata artifact here once done. :thumbsup:

vikram_r: uploaded cleaned metadata to their tenant and validated SAML flow end-to-end in staging. customer confirmed login succeeded after we applied the cleaned metadata. leaving follow-up to eng-saml for the permanent fix.

eng-saml: adding follow-up tasks to backlog: SAML-312 add xml:base handling, SAML-313 cert whitespace tolerance, SAML-314 normalization test-suite.

maria_g: closing loop with customer now. thanks team.
